findings.title: The name is voiced, glorified, and remembered
findings.claim: Across the host reading, the basmala's name of Allah is taken up as the Lord's name to glorify and later remember before prayer; the same explicit name Allah returns as the agent of will and knowledge around recitation.
findings.mechanism: The focus noun ism carries the ordinary sense of a name or designation. In 87:1 and 87:15 the host context makes a Lord's name the object of glorification and remembrance, with prayer following; this also meets the branch's source-attested account of a name raising its referent's mention. Separately, 87:7 repeats the focus proper name Allah as the one who wills and knows, attaching the opening's named referent to the surah's account of recitation. Together these contacts turn the opening formula into a name the host reading both voices in worship and predicates action of.
findings.reader_payoff: The prefatory formula becomes part of the surah's own movement of naming, glorifying, remembering, and praying, while its later account of recitation returns to the same named Allah.
findings.containment: The host context does not make the common noun name mean worship, establish the source's mention-raising explanation as a literal lexical entailment, or say that every Lord-title repeats Allah as a form. The link between the focus name and the Lord named in 87:1 and 87:15 is a host-context inference; the focus formula remains the basmala.

epistemic.reason: The focus wording, repeated name, and host-context acts are explicit in the packet. Their synthesis as one opening-to-worship-and-recitation movement is interpretive, especially where the host uses Lord rather than repeating the focus wording Allah.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: ad, adlandırma ve ad ya da nitelik bakımından denklik
branch_activations.facet_statement: Ad, bir varlığı tanıtan ve ondan söz etmeyi sağlayan söz veya anlamdır.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus noun ٱسْمِ in بِسْمِ carries the ordinary meaning of a name or designation.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The host text commands glorification of the Lord's name in 87:1 and later says that the Lord's name is remembered in 87:15, before prayer.
branch_activations.activation: The separate host occurrences take the focus's ordinary naming concept as an object of glorifying and remembering, making the prefatory name part of an enacted sequence rather than an unattached formula.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The opening name is heard within the host surah's own acts of naming, praise, and remembrance.
branch_activations.boundary: This is a within-surah lexical and contextual recurrence; it does not give the word name a different lexical meaning or establish that every Lord-reference is a repetition of Allah.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: ad, adlandırma ve ad ya da nitelik bakımından denklik
branch_activations.facet_statement: Kaynaklar adın kökenini, adı verilen şeyin anılmasını yükseltmesi ve onu belirgin kılmasıyla açıklar.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus noun ٱسْمِ carries the name concept whose source-attested explanation includes raising the named one's mention.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The first host ayah commands glorification and calls the Lord Most High; a later host ayah says the Lord's name is remembered.
branch_activations.activation: The glorifying command, the epithet Most High, and the later act of remembrance meet the branch's source-image of a name raising its referent's mention.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The prefatory name enters a host reading that explicitly elevates and remembers the Lord's name.
branch_activations.boundary: This activates the source-attested mention-raising image only; it does not make height the lexical meaning of ism or prove a historical etymology from this context.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Temel eylem, bir varlığa tapınmak ve kişinin kendini bu tapınmaya vermesidir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus proper name ٱللَّهِ supplies the named being in the opening formula.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The host surah commands glorification in 87:1 and ends the sequence of remembering the Lord's name with prayer in 87:15.
branch_activations.activation: The separate worship acts make the branch's act-of-worship facet relevant to the being named in the focus, while the proper name alone would not activate that facet.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The opening's named Allah is placed within the worship enacted by the host surah's glorification and prayer.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus proper noun does not itself mean worship; the contextual acts supply that relation, and the Lord-phrases are not morphological repetitions of the name Allah.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Eylemden türeyen varlık anlamı, kendisine tapınılan varlığı veya tapınma konusu sayılan nesneyi gösterir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus proper name ٱللَّهِ names the referent whom the host-context worship acts concern.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The host text's command to glorify and its statement that the Lord is prayed to provide the worship relation independently of the focus name.
branch_activations.activation: The context's glorification and prayer acts contact the focus referent as their worshiped being, so this extension is contextual rather than a claim that a proper name inherently means an object of worship.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The name at the opening is associated with the being toward whom the surah's praise and prayer are directed.
branch_activations.boundary: The association is limited to these supplied worship acts; it does not generalize this branch to every proper name or make the focus name itself an act.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: Yaratıcıya özgü ad ile seslenme ve ant biçimleri
branch_activations.facet_statement: Dalın merkezinde, Yaratıcıyı başkalarından ayırarak gösteren ve yalnız ona özgü sayılan özel ad bulunur.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus token ٱللَّهِ is the proper name of the Creator.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: After 87:6 says that the addressee will be made to recite and will not forget, 87:7 repeats Allah as the one whose will qualifies that statement and who knows what is public and hidden.
branch_activations.activation: The exact proper-name recurrence returns the focus name as an active referent in the host surah's account of recitation, will, and knowledge.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The opening's named Allah is connected to the one the host text names as governing an exception in recitation and knowing both what is voiced and what is hidden.
branch_activations.boundary: The packet supports this explicit repeated-name link; it does not make the basmala itself predict the recitation's details or treat every later Lord-title as an exact lexical repetition of Allah.

findings.title: Mercy is given a setting in creation and guidance
findings.claim: The host surah gives the opening's mercy epithets a concrete setting in the Lord's creating and forming, measuring and guiding, bringing out pasture, and making the easier course available.
findings.mechanism: The focus mercy forms carry the branch's core relation between compassion and active sparing or beneficence. The host verbs independently describe creation, formation, measure, guidance, pasture, and ease; placed beside the two mercy epithets, they make the active-care facet salient. The branch's God-specific facet then frames that care as goodness reaching created beings, while remaining a contextual application rather than a replacement definition.
findings.reader_payoff: The two opening mercy names are heard against acts of making, guiding, providing, and easing, rather than left as unattached attributes.
findings.containment: The contextual acts illustrate a mercy reading but do not make every event an act of mercy or promise universal ease. The pasture also becomes dry stubble, and the host surah includes severe warning and the fire in which the wretched neither die nor live (87:5, 87:11–13); those turns remain alongside the opening names.

epistemic.reason: The focus forms and the host actions are explicit in the packet. Reading the creative, guiding, and easing actions as the contextual realization of mercy is a supported interpretive relation, not an explicit equation stated by the host text.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bu iç yöneliş, acınan kişiyi esirgemeyi ve ona iyilikte bulunmayı gerektiren etkin bir sonuç taşır.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus adjectives ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ and ٱلرَّحِيمِ carry the mercy and tenderness field.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The host context says that the Lord creates and forms, measures and guides, brings out pasture, and makes an easier course available.
branch_activations.activation: These distinct acts of guidance, provision, and ease meet the branch's active-beneficence facet, giving the focus mercy forms a concrete host-context setting.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The opening's mercy is colored by the host surah's depiction of creative care, guidance, provision, and ease.
branch_activations.boundary: The contact does not establish that every act or outcome in the surah is merciful; it adds these particular acts as context for the focus epithets.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Tanrı hakkında kullanıldığında esirgemenin genişliği ve yaratılmışlara iyilik olarak ulaşması belirginleşir.
branch_activations.carrier: The two focus mercy epithets are applied to God in the basmala.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The host surah attributes making, guidance, pasture, and ease to the Lord and describes creation as its recipient.
branch_activations.activation: Because the focus uses the mercy branch for God, the host's acts of creating, guiding, providing, and easing activate its God-specific facet of goodness reaching created beings.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The epithets' divine mercy is read in the context of care that reaches creation through making, guidance, provision, and ease.
branch_activations.boundary: This is a bounded contextual realization, not a claim that the surah explicitly labels each act mercy or that its warnings and afterlife outcomes are removed.
